thread:
elaine_rm: Heads-up — deploy-bot blocked rc4. Two issues: vuln scan flagged a transitive dependency and SBOM provenance missing for an optimizer component. Change window closes in ~3h, need decision: pin, hotpatch, or full rollback.

deploy-bot: RELEASE 2026-03-10-rc4 BLOCKED by policy checks
policy:vuln-scan FAILED (transitive -> optimizer v0.9.3, CVE-2026-0456, severity: high, exploitability: low)
policy:sbom PROVENANCE WARNING (component 'optimizer' missing signature)

sam_dev: Can someone paste the dependency tree that triggered this? I think optimizer was pulled by builder-tool v2.4.

maria_sec: Triage summary: CVE is high severity but no public exploit or PoC we can see. Risk is supply-chain/backdoor angle because optimizer is unsigned in our SBOM. Legal also flagged license ambiguity.

ben_release: Quick options: 
1) Hotpatch — rebuild images pinning optimizer->0.9.2 and prod-republish (fastest if build pipeline is green)
2) Scoped rollback — only roll service-a that uses the new optimizer layer
3) Full rollback to rc3 (safest but disruptive to customers)

elaine_rm: Hotpatch looks attractive but SBOM signature missing means we still need to regenerate signed SBOMs and get the provenance check green. That adds ~60–90m to the hotpatch timeline. Any faster path?

qa_bot: Canary CI: integration tests failed intermittently on eu-west-1 after a local rebuild candidate. Re-running now.

sam_dev: Snagged the exact tree: `builder-tool@2.4.1 -> optimizer@0.9.3 -> libzip@1.6.2`
To inspect SBOM for optimizer: ```jq '.components[] | select(.name=="optimizer")' out/sbom.json```

maria_sec: Propose mitigation path if we want to ship: 
- Rebuild images pinning optimizer->0.9.2 (regenerates SBOM)
- Add runtime feature-flag to disable optimizer behavior (kill-switch)
- Add extra call-home monitoring for anomalies
- Legal to add a temporary license note in release notes
If all that lands within the change window, security will approve a temporary exception. :eyes:

legal: I can draft the release note language now. We need artifact-level acknowledgement and a follow-up remediation ticket assigned to platform-security. I can sign off on the note conditionally.

ben_release: Timeline estimate: 
- Rebuild + signed SBOM: ~75m (depends on queue)
- QA regression run: ~25–40m
- Release sign-off: ~10m
So optimistic ~100–130m. If queue backs up, fallback is full rollback.

elaine_rm: Ok. Decision path: We attempt the hotpatch+rebuild + feature-flag. If signed SBOM and green QA within 2h, proceed. Otherwise, rollback to rc3 at T+2h. Everyone ack?

maria_sec: Ack from security if we get the feature-flag and monitoring in place.

legal: Ack — I'll post the release note snippet in 15m.

sam_dev: Starting rebuild now and pinning optimizer->0.9.2, pushing to staging. Pinging infra to prioritize the build.

deploy-bot: Action: HOLD release (reason: policy block). Canary deployments paused.

ben_release: Noted — coordinating rollback window just in case.

elaine_rm: I'll update the release tracker and notify support. If anyone sees a regression in canary logs, ping here immediately. :thumbsup:

qa_bot: Regression rerun passed in eu-west-1 staging candidate. Will continue longer smoke run.

sam_dev: Build finished and SBOM re-generated & signed. Uploading artifacts to s3 and kicking off canary redeploy.

maria_sec: Security checks re-run: vuln-scan still flags optimizer but now it's pinned to 0.9.2 with no known CVEs. Provenance check: OK (signed). Security lifts hold pending green canary.

deploy-bot: RELEASE HOLD REMOVED — all policy checks green. Canary resume scheduled.

elaine_rm: Great. Proceeding with gradual roll now. Legal note added to the release notes. Closing thread unless new issues crop up.

ben_release: Thanks team. Will keep rollback playbook ready. :white_check_mark:
